notes.summary: Exact-version audit of all ten supplied caches: BFJ 1201.0188 is v1 with algebraizability and SNC-support restrictions; 1805.01016 is Boucksom--Eriksson's norms paper. The synthetic source proves measure-side completeness, not general E1 surjectivity. Actual PDFs resolve an OCR omission and a printed sign slip.
notes.detailedSummary: All ten supplied PDF and text hashes, and all six supplied abstract hashes, match. Each actual PDF was independently re-extracted successfully. The saved BFJ equation v1 Theorem A requires smooth projective geometry, a complete discrete field of residue characteristic zero, function-field algebraizability, raw degree mass, and support on one SNC dual complex. Its operator/comparison sections do not impose that target-support condition. The trivial-field source v4 states a genuine arbitrary-support finite-energy theorem in arbitrary dimension under smoothness and characteristic zero. Synthetic 2307.01697v1 supplies test orthogonality and quantitative estimates over projective Berkovich spaces but does not itself construct the general unbounded-potential theory. Actual PDF page 25 confirms absolute-value bars in synthetic (2.27); BFJ v1 page 28 confirms a printed sign error in Lemma 6.10, handled by a direct proof in n3. These are source observations and application checks, not an exhaustive literature theorem.
notes.text:
Only the input, fresh workspace, and ten authorized source caches were read. Running `python3 audit_sources.py > source-audit-output.txt 2>&1` gave one successful PDF re-extraction for each of 1201.0187, 1201.0188, 1805.01016, 1801.08229, 2307.01697, 2209.04879, 2506.13548, Thuillier, Berkovich, and 1204.6277; all supplied hash checks returned True. Literal proof extracts, independently regenerated PDF text, source identities, versions, hashes and exact application checks are retained in source-extracts/source-provenance.json. This is an artifact observation, not mathematical verification.

The actual 1201.0188v1 PDF hash is 4c29d91987477baf9baa4dfdd0b901ae1cd8910746012fd6285ab9a90bbf3f3a. Its banner is v1 dated 30 Dec 2011; its internal date is 29 Oct 2018. Theorem A, printed pages 2--3, requires X to be smooth projective and algebraizable over a complete discrete residue-characteristic-zero field, L ample, target mass c1(L)^n, and target supported on a dual complex of some SNC model. It concludes a continuous semipositive solution unique up to scaling. This is not an arbitrary-support statement, and the internal date does not justify treating these bytes as a later arXiv version. Sections 2--7 construct the genuine bounded and E1 operators, energy, locality and comparison in the smooth projective discrete residue-zero setting. Target support is unnecessary for those constructions; algebraizability is used in Appendix A's orthogonality argument and Theorem A's application. Proposition 8.2 states E1 uniqueness without orthogonality.

BFJ 1201.0187v2, PDF hash 8b684713055b9147de0d3379ad925c58f031bafe10a77e769a2791cdaa128270, supplies normalized PSH compactness (Theorem 7.10), the envelope property and continuous envelopes (Theorems 7.11 and 8.3), and decreasing model regularization (Theorem B/8.7) for smooth projective X, ample L, and complete discrete K with residue characteristic zero. It does not impose function-field algebraizability.

1805.01016v3, hash 51d02f75a65aa463f8e22393933f5ebef9036e322d720fc632f87759c2b71cb2, is Boucksom--Eriksson, Spaces of norms, determinant of cohomology and Fekete points in non-Archimedean geometry. Theorem 8.4 supplies the genuine continuous mixed MA operator and uniform-convergence continuity. It is not a differently titled pluripotential paper or a general unbounded E1 equation theorem.

1801.08229v4, hash 8d5975337f4ac88a475929ea6a436ec4a15d08715d5582bc0ba0eb3e07152c52, is Boucksom--Jonsson's Global pluripotential theory over a trivially valued field. Its Theorem A and Theorem 12.9 treat every finite-dual-energy probability measure under smoothness and either characteristic zero or dimension at most two. We use only the algebraically closed, trivially valued, characteristic-zero, smooth integral projective ample setting, in arbitrary dimension.

2307.01697v1, hash 979daddbb2082320cd6bbe6f8522535e68b56d229317decd033c3101b9fdbaa1, is the synthetic measures paper. Example 2.20 states test-function orthogonality for projective Berkovich spaces, using BE21 Theorem A and Boucksom--Gubler--Martin, Differentiability of relative volumes over an arbitrary non-Archimedean field, IMRN 2022 no. 8, 6214--6242, Lemma 3.2. This published background is used through the supplied source's explicit assertion; no extra BGM PDF was supplied or fetched. Smooth geometrically integral projective X is geometrically reduced, the ample class lies in Pos(X), and the semipositive model reference lies in Z+, so the stated application domain is satisfied. Theorem 1.26, Proposition 2.2, Theorem 2.23 and Lemma 2.25 provide the submean bound, coercivity, maximizing-test estimates and integral estimate used below. Theorem A/2.26 proves density and completeness on the measure side; Remark 2.14 sets aside the potential theory.

Actual PDF inspections are retained and rerendered by `python3 build_artifacts.py`: source-extracts/synthetic-page25.png verifies the absolute-value bars missing from OCR in (2.27); bfj-v1-page27.png verifies the truncation/full-mass estimate; bfj-v1-page28.png shows that Lemma 6.10's statement has a positive integral of -psi while its proof uses the negative integral of psi; bj-v4-page122.png verifies the compactness-and-attainment proof and Theorem 12.9. The printed sign slip cannot establish integrability by its displayed statement alone; n3 proves the required estimate directly.

Pille--Schneider 2209.04879v2 Remark 4.4 separates general-field definition of E1 from its generally unclear operator extension. Its phrase field characteristic zero is not used to remove BFJ's residue-characteristic restriction. Gubler--Rabinoff 2506.13548v2 explicitly leaves constructing MA outside its subject. Thuillier's HAL v1 thesis provides curve theory, not an unannounced general-dimension theorem. Berkovich's 1993 PMIHES paper is analytic/cohomological background, not preservation of unbounded energy or MA under base change. The actual CLD 1204.6277v2 is the July 2025 revision; no application of its local-current theory to all global BFJ E1 targets over arbitrary fields is established here. These last four are audit-only and are not substituted for missing global inputs.

notes.summary: Source-established arbitrary-support theorem at the trivial-field endpoint: smooth integral projective X over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, ample L, arbitrary dimension, raw mass (L^n), finite dual energy, genuine E1 MA and uniqueness modulo constants. This is partial for original P16.6.
notes.detailedSummary: Under precisely those retained hypotheses, Boucksom--Jonsson 1801.08229v4 constructs an approximation-independent genuine finite-energy mixed MA operator, and every positive Radon target of raw mass V=(L^n) with sup_u{V E(u)-integral u dmu}<infinity is its image. There is no skeletal-support or toric-invariance hypothesis. The proof uses the intersection pairing, envelope regularity and compactness, finite-energy differentiation, continuity of integration on bounded-energy sets, comparison and injectivity. The result is already in the supplied source and does not by itself prove a discrete or arbitrary-field endpoint.
notes.text:
Retain k algebraically closed, trivially valued and of characteristic zero; X/k smooth, connected, integral and projective of any dimension n>=1; L ample; and the canonical trivial-field reference metric. Set V=(L^n)>0. Let E be the normalized intersection energy with E(0)=0 and E(u+c)=E(u)+c, and E1={u psh:E(u)>-infinity}. On a positive Radon target require mu(Xan)=V and raw dual energy mathscrE(mu)=sup_{u in model/FS tests}{V E(u)-integral u dmu}<infinity. For the entire probability nu=mu/V this is V times Q(nu)=sup{E(u)-integral u dnu}. Only the whole target is normalized. Constants show the raw supremum is infinite if its mass differs from V.

This theorem is already established by 1801.08229v4, not a new extension. Theorem 7.1 extends the genuine intersection energy pairing by majorants, uniquely and decreasing-continuously. Theorem 7.8 makes mixed pairings finite on E1. Theorem 7.18 uses their values against PL functions to define the genuine mixed MA functional; positivity, its value V on constants, PL density, and Riesz give a unique positive Radon measure. Proposition 7.19 verifies the model intersection formula and decreasing continuity. Consequently all decreasing model approximations define the same raw operator M(u), of mass V. No inverse Banach measure construction or fixed skeleton is involved.

Theorem 5.20 supplies the envelope property under the stated smoothness and characteristic-zero hypotheses; Corollary 5.21 gives compact normalized PSH, and Lemma 5.17 gives continuous envelopes of continuous obstacles. Theorem 8.5/Corollary 8.6 gives differentiation of E(P(u+tf)) with derivative integral f d(M(u)/V). Theorem 9.20 identifies Q(nu)<infinity with integrability of every E1 potential. Proposition 9.19 proves L1(nu) continuity on bounded-energy sets. These are indispensable source inputs with checked domains, not assumed replacements over a different field.

To see surjectivity, normalize a model maximizing sequence for F_nu=E-integral against nu. Source estimate (9.11) bounds its energy. Compact normalized PSH gives a subnet limit u; energy upper semicontinuity keeps u in E1; Proposition 9.19 passes the nu-integrals to the limit. Thus u attains Q(nu), as in the actual printed proof of Theorem 12.8. Corollary 9.12 identifies the maximizer with M(u)/V=nu using differentiation. Necessity of finite dual energy follows from concavity and integrability of u against its own MA, with equality Q(M(u)/V)=E(u)-integral u d(M(u)/V). Theorems 7.40 and 7.44 give locality and comparison; Proposition 12.7 gives injectivity modulo constants. Theorem 12.9 states existence and uniqueness for every finite-energy target. Therefore the raw range is exactly the targets just specified, with no restriction on support.

The full application and remaining original obligations are written in P16.6-argument.md and the standalone P16.6-paper.tex/P16.6-paper.pdf. Rerun `python3 build_artifacts.py` for the paper. This is a general-dimension mathematical source theorem, not a finite computation. It is only a partial result for original P16.6: its trivial-field assumptions are not transported to another field by base change or by completeness of measures.

notes.summary: Proved deduction at the discrete residue-zero endpoint in arbitrary dimension: smooth geometrically integral projective X, ample L, every raw-mass-V finite-dual-energy Radon target, genuine E1 MA, comparison and uniqueness. The explicit test-to-E1 passage removes SNC support and avoids function-field algebraizability. It remains partial for original P16.6.
notes.detailedSummary: The argument combines the genuine BFJ v1 operator and the compactness/envelopes of BFJ 1201.0187v2 with the supplied synthetic orthogonality and integral estimates. It proves that synthetic test orthogonality becomes the classical continuous-envelope orthogonality at this endpoint; proves L1 continuity against an arbitrary finite-energy target on bounded-energy psh sets; establishes actual variational attainment; and differentiates through unbounded envelopes to obtain the actual MA equation. The exact raw measure condition is mass V=(L^n) and sup_{u in D_theta}{V E_theta(u)-integral u dmu}<infinity, equivalently E1 integrability after normalizing the whole measure. An actual printed sign slip in BFJ v1 Lemma 6.10 is bypassed by a direct integrability proof. The proof does not export BFJ compactness or envelopes to nondiscrete fields and makes no novelty claim.
notes.text:
Retain K complete and nontrivially discretely valued with residue characteristic zero (hence also field characteristic zero); X/K smooth, geometrically integral and projective, dimension n>=1 arbitrary; L ample; and a semipositive model reference with curvature theta. Normalize valuation units by -log|varpi|=1. No function-field algebraizability is imposed. Set V=(L^n)>0, M_theta(u) the raw genuine MA and m_theta(u)=M_theta(u)/V. Model M is the intersection measure sum_E b_E(L_u|E)^n delta_{x_E}, with mass V. Use normalized energy E(u)=1/((n+1)V) sum_{j=0}^n integral u(theta+ddc u)^j theta^{n-j}, extended by decreasing majorants, and E1={psh u:E(u)>-infinity}.

The theorem claims that M:E1/R -> {positive Radon mu:mu(Xan)=V, mathscrE(mu)<infinity} is a bijection, where mathscrE(mu)=sup_{a in D_theta}{V E(a)-integral a dmu}. Equivalently Q(nu)=sup_a{E(a)-integral a dnu}<infinity for the whole probability nu=mu/V. Constants force the correct raw mass. No toric, skeletal or dimension-one assumption occurs. This is a mathematical deduction from the source inputs in n1, not an assertion that BFJ v1 Theorem A already said this.

First construct the genuine operator. BFJ v1 Theorem 3.1 constructs the bounded mixed operator from intersections. Its locality allows M(u)=lim_{t->infinity}1_{u>-t}M(max(u,-t)), an increasing limit on Borel sets. For u<=0 in E1, the energy difference formula gives E(u_{t/2})-E(u_t)>=t m(u_t){u<=-t}/[2(n+1)]. Decreasing energy continuity makes the discarded mass o(1/t), so M(u) has full raw mass V. BFJ Lemma 6.8 gives the truncation bound |integral f dm(u_t)-integral f dm(u)|<=2(n+1)|E(u)| ||f||_infinity/t. Proposition 6.9 gives continuity along any decreasing E1 net, and model-test density therefore proves approximation independence. For applying the source's unit-volume normalization, lambda=V^{-1/n}, theta_tilde=lambda theta and u_tilde=lambda u satisfy M_tilde(lambda u)=M(u)/V and E_tilde(lambda u)=lambda E(u); truncations and cones correspond. Proposition 6.11 supplies genuine E1 locality and comparison, integral_{u<v}M(v)<=integral_{u<v}M(u). Proposition 8.2 supplies uniqueness modulo constants without orthogonality or target support.

The actual v1 PDF statement of Lemma 6.10 has a sign slip, so prove the needed integrability. For finite-energy u,v<=0 and w=(u_t+v_s)/2, bounded energy and positive mixed measures give E((u+v)/2)<=E(w)<=integral w dm(w)/(n+1)<=2^{-(n+1)} integral v_s dm(u_t)/(n+1)<=2^{-(n+1)} integral_{u>-t} v_s dm(u)/(n+1). The penultimate inequality uses m(w)>=2^{-n}m(u_t) and w<=v_s/2; the last uses locality and discards a nonpositive integral. Let s and then t increase through integers. Since m(u) is carried by {u finite}, sequential monotone convergence gives integral v dm(u)>-infinity, bounded below by (n+1)2^{n+1}E((u+v)/2). Concavity makes the lower bound finite. Constants handle unnormalized u,v. This proves the required integrability without using the erroneous displayed bound.

Next replace algebraizability-based orthogonality. Synthetic Example 2.20/Definition 2.15 says lim_{a in D_theta,a<f} integral(f-a)dm(a)=0 for model f, with the directed pointwise order. BFJ 1201.0187v2 Theorem 8.3 makes P(f) continuous in the retained discrete setting. Decreasing model approximants to P(f) are uniform by Dini; shifting them down slightly makes them strictly below f. Thus the entire increasing directed test net has supremum P(f) and converges uniformly by Dini. BE Theorem 8.4 passes genuine MA to the limit, yielding integral(f-P(f))dm(P(f))=0. Uniform density of model f, the 1-Lipschitz envelope property and uniform-convergence continuity of continuous MA extend this to every continuous obstacle. This is precisely BFJ v1's classical orthogonality hypothesis. Theorem 7.2/Corollary 7.3 then yields d/dt|_0 E(P(u+tf))=integral f dm(u) for every u in E1 and continuous f, including unbounded u.

Here is the indispensable passage to arbitrary target support. Put m0=m(0), J(u)=integral u dm0-E(u), and r_nu(a)=Q(nu)-E(a)+integral a dnu. Synthetic (2.7) gives J(a)<=C_n(r_nu(a)+Q(nu)); the submean theorem gives sup u-integral u dm0<=T. On sup u=0, -E(u)<=J(u)+T. Finite Q implies E1 integrability against nu: for decreasing model majorants a_alpha->u, duality bounds integral a_alpha dnu from below by E(a_alpha)-Q. The BFJ Radon/usc-net integration lemma passes this bound to u. Energy continuity also proves Q=sup_{u in E1}(E(u)-integral u dnu). No unrestricted monotone-convergence theorem for arbitrary nets is assumed.

Choose maximizing model tau_j for Q, so r_nu(tau_j)->0 and J(tau_j) is bounded. Synthetic Lemma 2.25(2.27), whose absolute-value bars were verified in the PDF, gives for model a with bounded J the uniform bound |integral a(dnu-dm(tau_j))|<=C_R r_nu(tau_j)^{1/2}. This follows by using its second test potential zero, J(a,0) comparable to J(a), and fixing an energy bound R for a, tau_j and nu. For a in E1, decreasing model majorants have J converging to J(a), since m0 has finite divisorial support and energies converge. Their integrals against nu and m(tau_j) converge, so the same estimate extends to all E1 with bounded J, uniformly in a.

If u_i->u in BFJ's psh topology and J(u_i) is bounded, lower semicontinuity of J makes u finite energy. For fixed j the model measure m(tau_j) has finite divisorial support, so its integral of u_i converges to that of u. The uniform estimate just proved, followed by j->infinity, gives convergence of the nu-integrals. For L1 convergence use w_i=max(u_i,u). Supremums and m0-integrals are bounded on a convergent psh net, energies of u_i are bounded below, monotonicity bounds energies of w_i below, and therefore J(w_i) is bounded. Divisorial values give w_i->u. Applying integral convergence to w_i and u_i and the identity |u_i-u|=2w_i-u_i-u proves L1(nu) convergence. This includes the subnet used in the variational proof.

A normalized model maximizing sequence now has bounded J and energy. BFJ normalized-PSH compactness yields a psh subnet limit u; energy upper semicontinuity keeps u in E1. The proved L1 lemma yields F_nu(u)>=limsup F_nu(u_i)=Q(nu), hence equality. This is actual attainment. For continuous f, v_t=P(u+tf) lies in E1 because it dominates u-|t| ||f||, and it remains below its usc obstacle. Maximality gives E(v_t)-E(u)<=integral(v_t-u)dnu<=t integral f dnu. Divide for both signs of t and use the finite-energy envelope derivative. Then integral f dm(u)=integral f dnu for all continuous f, so equality of genuine Radon measures gives M(u)=mu.

Conversely, the genuine full mass and concavity/segment differentiation imply Q(m(u))=E(u)-integral u dm(u)<infinity; the integrability bound above makes it finite, and decreasing approximation gives equality at the supremum. Thus the raw range is exact. For reference change theta'=theta+ddc h by a bounded semipositive model potential, transformed approximants give M_theta'(u-h)=M_theta(u), E_theta'(u-h)=E_theta(u)-E_theta(h), and Q_theta'(nu)=Q_theta(nu)+integral h dnu-E_theta(h). Hence energy finiteness and the equation are reference-independent.

The precise dual condition is also equivalent in this setting to E1 subset L1(nu). For the converse, integrability forces a uniform bound on -integral a dnu for normalized model tests J(a)<=1: otherwise a sequence with integrals <=-2^j gives a decreasing convex series sum 2^{-j}a_j of energy >=-(1+T), hence an E1 limit with integral minus infinity, a contradiction. Synthetic J(ta)<=C_n t^2J(a) then bounds -integral a dnu by A(1+sqrt(C_nJ(a))). Since E(a)<=-J(a), its dual supremum is finite. The energy and derivative calculations retain the original ample datum and raw mass.

The complete proof is P16.6-argument.md, also embedded in standalone P16.6-paper.tex and P16.6-paper.pdf. Rerun `python3 build_artifacts.py`. This is a proof draft using explicitly applied source inputs, not a finite calculation or a conditional template. It remains partial for original P16.6: over nondiscrete fields the geometric compactness and continuous-envelope passages used here have not been supplied or proved.

notes.text:
The implementation assignment produced P16.6-argument.md containing the full proof and concrete gaps, standalone P16.6-paper.tex, and P16.6-paper.pdf. The positive mathematical results are n2 and n3 under their exact retained hypotheses. They cover every positive raw-mass-V finite-dual-energy Radon measure with genuine MA, not only invariant or skeleton-supported targets, in arbitrary dimension. Neither is declared a complete solution of original P16.6.

The original residual arbitrary-field support atom remains unproved even when smooth projective geometrically integral geometry and ample L are retained. For general complete nontrivially valued, potentially nondiscrete fields, this work does not construct an approximation-independent genuine unbounded mixed operator with full raw mass; establish normalized global psh compactness and envelope regularity or an effective alternative; prove finite-energy differentiation for the actual unbounded operator; prove locality/comparison and uniqueness modulo constants there; or prove attainment/realization for every raw-mass-V finite-dual-energy target. These are specific missing mathematical passages, not claims that no theorem can ever exist. The supplied trivial-field Theorem 12.8 makes potential completeness and surjectivity equivalent to an envelope property; the synthetic completeness theorem concerns measures instead. Dense test images in a complete measure space do not alone realize them by global psh potentials.

No retraction-factorization claim, reduction to one skeleton, silent curve or projective-line assumption, alternate inverse measure, or unproved base-change/alteration/normalization/resolution preservation theorem was used. Singular geometry, positive residue characteristic, nonample classes, proper nonprojective spaces and nonalgebraizable spaces remain the separate original atoms.

Inputs are preserved as byte-identical input.json and input-original.json, decoded assignment-original.txt and task-original.json. Source-extracts/source-provenance.json records all ten exact cache versions/hashes, literal published proof extracts, fresh text from actual PDFs, source application checks, published-background provenance and four rendered-PDF inspections. Environment/tool details are in environment.json. status.json has exactly id,status,exact_result,proof_file,concrete_gaps, with status partial. Canonical notes and candidate=false are retained in notes.json.
